original_question: Given an (Abelian) group G viewed as the symmetry measure space (G, asdim, S) with central symmetries, calculate or estimate its dimension symmetry numbers mds_r(G).
target_in_paper: Problem 11.2 in §11: "Given an (Abelian) group G calculate or evaluate its dimension symmetry numbers mds_r(G)."
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly points to the group version in §11, uses the paper’s notation mds_r(G), places G in the symmetry-measure-space framework (G, asdim, S), and focuses on central symmetries rather than drifting to the neighboring centerpole-number problem.
missing_details: It should be identified explicitly as the open problem stated in Problem 11.2, not as a theorem or conjecture.
The paper does not restrict the problem to Abelian groups; it says "(Abelian)" to indicate a particularly important subcase, but the ambient question is for arbitrary groups.
The family of admissible symmetries must be defined precisely: S = {s_c : c ∈ G}, where s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c; in additive Abelian notation this becomes s_c(x) = 2c − x.
The notation mds_r(G) should be unpacked as ms_r(G, asdim, S).
The parameter r ranges over cardinals r ≥ 1, not merely over finite integers.
Because in §11 the measure asdim is defined on the whole power set P(G), the relevant colorings are arbitrary r-colorings χ:G→r; there is no additional measurability restriction here.
A subset A ⊂ G should be defined to be centrally symmetric when A = s_c(A) for some c ∈ G.
The asymptotic-dimension measure asdim on subsets of G must be stated, since without it the invariant mds_r(G) is not stand-alone.
The value range of asdim is [-1, ∞], and finite subsets are exactly those with asdim(A) = -1.
The draft does not distinguish the full evaluation problem from the weaker nearby existence question solved in part by Theorem 11.1, namely when mds_r(G) ≥ 0 for infinite Abelian groups.
refined_question: Let G be a group (in particular, one may focus on the Abelian case) and let S = {s_c : c ∈ G} be the family of central symmetries, where s_c(x) = c x^{-1} c (equivalently, s_c(x) = 2c − x in additive Abelian notation). Regard G as the symmetry measure space (G, asdim, S), where asdim:P(G)→[-1,∞] is the asymptotic-dimension measure defined by: asdim(A) ≤ n if and only if for every finite subset F ⊂ G there exists a cover 𝒰 of A with finite mesh(𝒰) = ⋃_{U∈𝒰} U^{-1}U such that, for some finite subset B ⊂ G, each x ∈ G \ B has xF meeting at most n+1 members of 𝒰; equivalently, finite subsets are exactly those with asdim = -1. For each cardinal r ≥ 1, calculate or estimate the dimension symmetry number mds_r(G) := ms_r(G, asdim, S), i.e. determine or bound the quantity mds_r(G) = inf_{χ:G→r} sup_{i∈r, c∈G} asdim(χ^{-1}(i) ∩ s_c(χ^{-1}(i))).
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for each cardinal r ≥ 1, determine the threshold λ = mds_r(G) such that every r-coloring χ:G→r contains a monochromatic centrally symmetric subset A ⊂ G with asdim(A) ≥ λ, while for every λ' > λ there exists an r-coloring with no monochromatic centrally symmetric subset of asymptotic dimension at least λ'.
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact open problem stated in Problem 11.2 of §11, and not at a broader neighboring question. Section 11 specializes the general symmetry-measure-space framework to groups endowed with the asymptotic-dimension measure and the family of central symmetries, and introduces the notation mds_r(G) = ms_r(G, asdim, S). Section 3 supplies the general definition of ms_r(X), and because the central symmetries are involutive, this yields the concrete inf-sup formula used above. Theorem 11.1, immediately preceding Problem 11.2, only gives a partial existence criterion for infinite Abelian groups, namely when mds_r(G) ≥ 0; it does not replace the full evaluation problem. Theorem 9.1 provides the main nearby solved model case, showing that for Euclidean and lattice examples one has mds_r(R^n) = mds_r(Z^n) = n − r + 1, which clarifies the intended meaning of the invariant but is not itself the target question.
